# The actual proper source class is not a Frobenius eigenclass in the specified weak ring

Joint AUTHOR manuscript: EM-PUBLIC-7CDA51 and EM-DIRECT-88303D. FROZEN_UNREVIEWED_JOINT_AUTHOR_PROOF. Both authors completed a common whole-manuscript self-check; this immutable whole unit awaits a genuine third-person review. It is not Source-published or Native-accepted. No scientific program, import, sample, coefficient computation by software, enumeration, consumer, new Task or Native vote is used.

The new calculation concerns the particular proper Frobenius and selected triangular full-extension shape of the old source-row interface. It does not deny a geometric Frobenius or a comparison in a larger ring. Historical papers, their genuine nonauthor reviews and their then-UNKNOWN statements are unchanged. The exact dependencies, limited classical imports and both authors' contributions are pinned in the separate context.

The Heartbeat native X6 project basis is retained. This is a separately typed external arithmetic/module argument: r and z are algebraic coordinates, not native spatial axes or physical time. The full proper, Kummer, baseline and extension channels remain in the old exact lifting criterion; the scalar elimination and row cokernel below are reversible arithmetic presentations, not a quotient of the project's state or operations.

## 1. Statement, rings and variance

Fix an allowed prime p congruent to13 or19 modulo24, an unramified complete DVR O with perfect residue field, K=O[1/p], and its specified isometric Witt coefficient map sigma. Put

    S=4r^3-3r, f=1-r^2, q=4r^2-1, P=fq,
    A=2S-1, B=4S-5,
    D=(1/(2P))*[[A,1],[B,-A]],
    w=(8r^p-4r)/f,
    Dalg=O[r,f^-1,q^-1], R=Dalg^dagger[1/p].                 (1)

Here D is the original period/solution-column connection matrix; Dalg is a ring. The weak completion is the actual embedded weak ring in its p-completion, with integral presentations sum_l p^l P_l in the displayed algebraic generators and degrees at most C(l+1). A finite p denominator is allowed in R. These are the exact rings of the actual properweak theorem, not an assertion that a p-completed localization is a Laurent-series ring.

Use theta(r)=1+(r-1)^p and phi(r)=r^p, with sigma applied to coefficients once. For psi one of these let Dpsi=psi' sigma(D)(psi), and let Mpsi be the actual undivided proper cohomological Frobenius in the corrected basis e=(omega,eta) of the literal family

    y^2=x^3+3(4S-5)x+4S^2-28S+22.                         (2)

The frozen actual properweak theorem supplies Mpsi in Mat2(Dalg^dagger), det Mpsi=p, specified by its canonical finite crystalline maps and common strong completion. Put Gpsi=Mpsi^-T. Then

    Gpsi'=D Gpsi-Gpsi Dpsi.                               (3)

The saved row basis has nabla(e)=e C dr with C=D^T. Thus a source row b couples to a period column y by by, and its differential is L_D(b)=b'+bD. This fixes every transpose below.

Our proposed theorem is

    [a] != lambda Phi_psi([a]) for EVERY lambda in K^*,
    a=w e1 dr, e1=(1,0),
    Phi_psi(b dr)=psi' sigma(b)(psi) Mpsi^T dr,              (4)

in R^(1x2)dr / {L_D(h)dr:h in R^(1x2)}. The pullback in (4) includes the base one-form, not only the coefficient object.
It is well-defined on this cokernel: cohomological horizontality gives
L_D(sigma(h)(psi)Mpsi^T)=psi' sigma(L_D(h))(psi)Mpsi^T.

Equivalently the OLD selected full-row equation has no weak solution:

    h'+h Dpsi=w e1 Gpsi-lambda psi' w(psi)e1.               (5)

Indeed multiply (5) on the right by Gpsi^-1 and use (3). Its left side becomes L_D(h Gpsi^-1), while its right side becomes a-lambda Phi_psi(a). Multiplication by Gpsi^-1 is an invertible weak row map. The old full-extension interface separately fixes the Kummer diagonal a0=p lambda and its bottom scalar/baseline equation. Failure of its necessary proper-source row (5) rules out THAT selected full extension for every baseline lift g, including g not sigma-fixed. It supplies no assertion about all rank-four comparisons, altered proper blocks, arbitrary gauges, unrestricted p-completion, geometric source objects or original observations/functionals.

The old full rank-four weak Taylor theorem and its bottom-row class transport identify (5) for theta and phi with the SAME lambda; the actual proper theorem identifies their proper blocks. Consequently we test theta at r=1 and phi at infinity. Raw phi is not being substituted as a log lift at the node. This consumes the old full class isomorphism; it is not a new assertion of singular-boundary lift invariance.

## 2. Differential restrictions of actual weak elements

At t=r-1 or z=1/r, let E_x^int be the p-complete bounded Laurent coefficient ring: coefficients belong to O and the negative coefficients tend to zero p-adically. Its coefficient Gauss norm is at most1 on each original generator. At the node all other removed points have p-unit differences; in particular f^-1=-1/(t(t+2)). At infinity

    r=z^-1, f^-1=-z^2/(1-z^2), q^-1=z^2/(4-z^2).

Thus Dalg maps continuously into E_x^int, and so does its p-completion. This statement alone makes NO arbitrary completed element a function on a boundary annulus.

For a weak presentation sum p^l P_l of degree at most C(l+1), on rho<=|x|<1 each generator has size at most rho^-c for a fixed c. Choose rho<1 sufficiently close to1 that |p| rho^-cC<1. The l-th term is bounded by |p|^l rho^-cC(l+1), hence converges geometrically on every closed subannulus. This defines R->Robba_x. Two presentations agree by their common Laurent coefficients in E_x[1/p]. Differentiation is compatible: on a closed subannulus a Laurent derivative multiplies coefficients by integers, of norm at most1, and changes the norm by at most rho^-1. The same geometric bound permits termwise differentiation. For z use d/dr=-z^2 d/dz. These are differential ring maps, not just maps of sets of formal series.

A matrix analytic and invertible on every |x|<1 multiplies a Robba row on a common annulus, even if its positive coefficients are not bounded. Laurent residue there is well-defined and Res(dv)=0. This is why full open-disc convergence of the local flat frames below suffices; no weak membership of those frames is assumed.

## 3. Exact row elimination and a rational infinity period

The identity S^2-1=-fq^2 and S'=3q give the displayed D. For h=(u,v) and source b=(b1,b2), the second equation of L_D(h)=b gives

    u=-2P v'+A v+2P b2.

Since A'=6q and A^2+B=-4Pq, the first equation then becomes

    -2 K(v)=b1-2(Pb2)'-A b2,
    K(v)=(P v')'-2qv.                                    (6)

This is reversible: subtract L_D(2P b2,0) first, then use the displayed u. It is an equivalent scalar presentation of the old row cokernel, not a separate discovery. For every integer j direct differentiation gives

    K(r^j)=-4(j+1)(j+2)r^(j+2)
           +(5j(j+1)+2)r^j-j(j-1)r^(j-2).                (7)

There is a unique even formal solution

    v0=r^-2 sum_(k>=0)c_k r^-2k,
    c0=1, c1=1/2,
    c_k=((20k^2-10k+2)c_(k-1)
         -(2k-2)(2k-1)c_(k-2))/(8k(2k+1)), k>=2.         (8)

This follows by comparing r^-2k in (7), with nonzero characteristic-zero denominators. All c_k are positive rational numbers in the ordinary real order: if c_(k-1)>=c_(k-2)/2>0, its numerator is at least (12k^2+2k-2)c_(k-1). This is at least half its denominator times c_(k-1), since the difference is (2k-2)(2k+1)>=0. Induction starts with c1=c0/2. This real positivity says nothing about p-adic signs or growth of the infinite sequence.

The corresponding formal horizontal period is

    y0=(v0,2P v0'-A v0)^T, y0'=D y0,
    y0,1=r^-2+..., y0,2=8r+....                           (9)

Writing p=2m+1, the exact finite identity

    w=4r/f-8 sum_(j=0)^(m-1)r^(2j+1)

and (8) show

    Res_infinity(w v0 dr)=8 sum_(k=0)^(m-1)c_k !=0.       (10)

The rational term (4r/f)v0 has order at most r^-3; the polynomial part has r^-1 coefficient -8 sum c_k, and dr=-z^-2 dz fixes the sign. Only finitely many rational coefficients enter. The denominators in (8) through k=m-1 are p-units, but nonzero reduction modulo p of the SUM is neither claimed nor needed. Equation(10) becomes a legal functional on all weak rows only after Sections5-6.

## 4. The actual node test forces lambda=p^-2

Use the old9897B theorem for the EXACT proper gauge H(t): H0=I,

    H'=D H-HN/t,
    N=(1/12)*[[-1,-1],[1,1]].                             (11)

H and H^-1 converge throughout the original |t|<1; this is the matched proper block of that theorem, not nilpotent-residue integrality used as a generic convergence rule. Thus on every weak row we may define

    res_1(b dr)=[Res_t(bH dt)] in K^(1x2)/K^(1x2)N.        (12)

It kills L_D(h)dr: after multiplication by H that differential is d(hH)+(hH)N dt/t. The first term has zero residue, the second lies in the indicated row image. No arbitrary completed primitive has entered a Robba pairing.

The actual Mtheta is regular over O[[t]]. This is its finite proper B_n construction, followed by its literal p-limit and t-evaluation. The weak matrix has that SAME bounded Laurent expansion: its specified common-completion equality and the coefficient maps Dalg^hat->E_t and B^hat->O[[t]] give equality for this particular matrix. An arbitrary weak element is not assigned a regular boundary value.

For clarity in the cohomology frame (kappa=omega+eta,eta), the cohomology residue is E12/12, whereas the period residue is E21/12. The old actual central graph theorem and actual proper basis/jump comparison show that canonical Mtheta(0) fixes kappa. The old determinant p then gives

    Mtheta(0)=[[1,b],[0,p]]                              (13)

in that frame. b is wholly unspecified; the new Tate calculation of b is NOT an input. The row residue quotient is the proper coefficient space modulo the graph line; (13) acts on it by p.

Here the formula for the regular actual comparison is exact, not a guessed boundary normalization. Set C(t)=H(t)^-1 Gtheta(t) H(t^p); all are regular near0. Horizontality gives C'=NC/t-pCN/t. Thus n C_n=N C_n-p C_n N. The operator on the right is nilpotent; for every n>=1, nI minus that operator is invertible in characteristic zero. Hence C_n=0 for n>=1 and C(t)=C0, with NC0=pC0N. Since H0=I, C0=Gtheta(0). The same identity holds analytically on the open disc by its exact Taylor coefficients. The proper data and H descend to Qp, so sigma(H)=H.

It follows that for a general row

    res_1(Phi_theta b)=p sigma(res_1 b) Mtheta(0)^T        (14)

on the residue quotient. The residue vector and the matrix in (14) are always in the SAME frame: (12) initially uses (omega,eta); simultaneous change to the frame of (13) makes its quotient action p. The first p is the pullback of dt/t under t->t^p. The actual source has only a simple pole here: Res(wdt)=-2 and H0=I. Therefore res_1(a)=-2[e1], a nonzero Qp-rational quotient vector (row im N is span(1,1)). Its sigma is itself. Combining (4), (13), (14) gives

    res_1(a)=lambda p^2 res_1(a), hence lambda=p^-2.       (15)

The quotient has dimension one over K, so cancellation of its nonzero vector is legitimate. No claim concerning all sigma-semilinear eigenvectors follows.

## 5. Actual good infinity and its canonical comparison

At z=1/r rescale the SAME curve by x=r^2 X,y=r^3 Y. It is

    Y^2=X^3+a_inf(z)X+b_inf(z),
    a_inf=48z-36z^3-15z^4,
    b_inf=64-96z^2-112z^3+36z^4+84z^5+22z^6.             (16)

At0 it is E0:Y^2=X^3+64, with discriminant -2^16*3^3, a p-unit. Let Cbase=Zp[z,Delta_inf^-1]. The family is smooth proper there. After coefficient extension the ordinary common algebraic open is

    (Cbase tensor_Zp O)[z^-1]=Dalg[r^-1].                (17)

Indeed Delta_old=-6912(S-1)(S+1)^3; its pullback factors at r=1,-1,1/2,-1/2 with p-unit leading constants, and Delta_inf=z^12 Delta_old(1/z). With z inverted, inverting Delta_inf inverts precisely all these factors. This proves (17) before any completion.

The corrected proper classes transform by

    e_old=e_inf J, J=diag(z,z^-1),
    e_inf=(Omega,X Omega), Omega=dX/(2Y).                (18)

This is relative differentiation (z is a base scalar), including the saved infinity primitive for the second-kind class. Specifically the old primitive y/x becomes rY/X, so its corrected class rescales by r exactly; no holomorphic shift is introduced. The proper basis computation from the literal cubic applies over Cbase/p^n: the same finite quadratic cover/coherent principal part and corrected eta give a free rank-two basis, H0 the base and free H2 with its unit trace class. Its connection Dinf is regular at z=0.

The base lift z->z^p exists on Cbase/p^n: substituted Delta is a unit modulo p and p is nilpotent. The SAME canonical unit crystalline pullback therefore has a finite proper matrix Minf,n in that basis. The old proper embedding/PD/cochain construction applies here with no nodal log step: local smooth Frobenius lifts on affine refinements and their common PD products represent the canonical pullback; corrected proper classes and reductions commute. Cup/trace compatibility gives determinant p in the p-torsion-free limit. More explicitly the old trace proof's top local dlog generator pulls back by p, its PD correction is exact, and the constant unit is preserved. The proper alternating pairing of Omega and corrected XOmega is the same unit pairing, so its rank-two multiplier is det Minf=p. This uses an actual finite complex and its canonical map, not horizontality as a uniqueness theorem for a guessed Frobenius.

Consequently Minf lies in Mat2(Cbase^hat), det p. Its evaluation in Zp[[z]] is integral and regular; at0 it is the actual crystalline pullback F* on H1 of E0. On (17), coordinate isomorphism and functoriality of the actual finite crystalline embedding complexes identify the two matrices:

    Mphi,old=J(z)^-1 Minf J(z^p).                        (19)

First make this comparison at every finite p-level on the common algebraic localization, then take the compatible coefficient limit, then its map to E_z. The actual properweak common-completion theorem identifies its matrix with precisely this matrix there. Thus the weak phi matrix has the Robba restriction of the ACTUAL good-family matrix in (19). We have not commuted localization with an inverse limit or upgraded arbitrary completed elements to Robba functions.

## 6. The good-point flat frame and its residue transformation

Put Ginf=Minf^-T. Its entries, and those of its inverse, are bounded power series after a finite p denominator, hence analytic on |z|<1. The regular rational connection Dinf has a unique normalized formal solution

    Hinf'=Dinf Hinf, Hinf(0)=I.                          (20)

It has a positive convergence radius: on some closed disc the connection coefficients are bounded, and the ordinary coefficient recursion is bounded by a fixed exponential divided by n!, giving a strictly positive radius. The inverse has the same local existence. Actual Frobenius horizontality and initial values give the formal identity

    Hinf(z)=Ginf(z) Hinf(z^p) Ginf(0)^-1.                (21)

All normalized geometric connection coefficients descend to Qp (indeed their formal coefficients are rational), so coefficient sigma is identity on Hinf. Equation(21) extends a solution/inverse on radius delta<1 to radius delta^(1/p). The extensions agree by the unique formal solution. Iteration proves Hinf and Hinf^-1 analytic on every |z|<1; no bound uniform up to the circle is asserted. Equivalently a maximal radius R0<1 contradicts (21), whose right side has radius at least R0^(1/p)>R0.

For every weak proper-valued one-form expressed in the good basis define

    R_inf(b dz)=Res_z(b Hinf dz) in K^(1x2).             (22)

Section2 makes this a genuine annular pairing. It kills all L_Dinf derivatives. From (21) and Minf^T=Ginf^-1 one obtains, for arbitrary K coefficients,

    R_inf(Phi_phi b)=p sigma(R_inf(b)) Minf(0)^T.         (23)

Indeed after multiplying by Hinf the integrand is p z^(p-1) sigma(bHinf)(z^p) Minf(0)^T dz, and substitution multiplies residue by p. Omitting sigma in (23) would be false in the stated general coefficient field.

The source a in the good basis is

    ((8z^(1-p)-4)/(1-z^2),0) dz.                        (24)

The formal period (9) in this basis is (z^-1 v0,z(2Pv0'-Av0))^T, with initial value (0,8). Regularity and uniqueness in (20) identify it with Hinf(z)(0,8)^T, not with a fictitious independent boundary functional. Its first component is z sum c_k z^(2k); the transformed upper-right connection coefficient has value1/8 at0, consistently giving that normalization. Therefore (10) states

    R_inf(a) (0,8)^T=8 sum_(k=0)^(m-1)c_k !=0.           (25)

In particular R_inf(a) is nonzero. Crucially the coefficients of Dinf, Hinf and (24) are rational; (24) has only a finite principal part. Thus its residue uses a finite rational jet and belongs to Q^2, in particular Qp^2, and sigma fixes it. This particular rationality, NOT an assertion about general vectors in (23), is used below. The original full-system parameter g has not entered this proper row.

## 7. The actual good-fiber Frobenius has no eigenvalue p

Let F be the Frobenius endomorphism of E0/Fp. It is pointed and has degree p, whereas [p] has degree p^2. Consequently u=F-[p] is not the zero endomorphism. It is a nonconstant pointed morphism of smooth proper elliptic curves, hence an isogeny. Over Fp the classical finite group-scheme kernel factorization gives an isogeny v with v u=[n] for a nonzero integer n. This does not replace group-scheme kernels by geometric points when p divides a degree.

Here are the cohomological facts needed for that elementary argument in the actual realization. Take the constant smooth good lift Y^2=X^3+64 over Zp and its product. The same smooth proper embedding complexes compute H0=Zp and H1 free of rank2, with its free top trace term. On the product E0 x E0, use product affine embedding covers. The de Rham complex is their derived tensor, because relative differentials on the smooth product split into the two factors and the common embedding comparisons are natural. Its degree-one Kunneth map is therefore the direct sum of the two H1 factors: no Tor term appears, since those proper cohomology modules are free. Restriction to the two pointed axes identifies these two summands. The actual embedding comparison is natural for arbitrary special-fiber morphisms; F, u and v need not have chosen global scheme lifts to this constant model.

The addition map restricts to the identity on both axes. Its H1 pullback is therefore (x,x). For any pointed maps f,g:E0->E0, composition of addition with (f,g) gives (f+g)^*=f^*+g^*. In particular [n]^*=nI for every integer n, also when p divides n. These maps and equalities use the same canonical crystalline functor, by the actual embedding-complex naturality; they are not inferred from a chosen scheme Frobenius lift.

It follows that u*=F*-pI and that u* v*=nI. After p inversion n is nonzero in Qp and invertible. Thus u* is invertible. In the actual good basis,

    Minf(0)-pI is invertible over Qp, and hence over K.   (26)

The only new classical imports here are Milne, Elliptic Curves, second edition, II1.5-1.8 (printed49: pointed isogenies and finite group-scheme factorization), IV9.1 (printed148-149: degree of Frobenius), and V7.3 and its following paragraph (printed216: degree p versus [p] degree p^2). Exact actual primary bytes and selected-page reading are recorded separately. No Hasse trace estimate, point count, classification of ordinary/supersingular cases or computed eigenvalue is used.

## 8. Assembly and exact boundary

Suppose (4), or equivalently (5), held over R for some lambda. Transport to the theta presentation and apply the node test: (15) gives lambda=p^-2. Transport with the SAME lambda to phi and apply (22)-(23). By (25) its residue R0=R_inf(a) is nonzero, and its rationality fixes sigma(R0)=R0. Hence

    R0=p^-2 p R0 Minf(0)^T,
    R0 Minf(0)^T=p R0,

contradicting (26). This proves the proposed non-proportionality and the failure of the necessary selected weak full-extension row.

The proof does not say that a general semilinear p-eigenvector cannot exist over K; it uses a particular rational residue. It does not move the raw phi lift into a nodal log chart. It does not force a strong-completion primitive to be an annular function. It does not prove that every matrix in the unrestricted p-completion is weak. The old unrestricted completed source-row proportionality, first actual full rank-four comparison in another ring or shape, source action, origin selection for an independent g, source functional/evaluation, original Y/Z/kappa, all-gauge or geometric nonexistence, global sign and mother Goal remain outside the theorem.

This is one new source-specific obstruction unit, not a new general Tool or two independent discoveries. Prior full Taylor and old row-cokernel interface are consumed, not re-proved as new results. The scalar recurrence's real positivity is only a proof of nonzero finite rational residue. The two local canonical comparison/analytic bridges are substantive new parts of this joint paper and require a genuine independent whole-proof review. Neither author claims PAPER_PASS on this draft.
